title: Dijkstra's shortest paths
summary: Always settle the closest unsettled vertex next, then see if going through it shortens the way to its neighbours.

checkpoints.text: The edges have weights (distances). Every vertex starts at ∞ except the start, 0, at distance 0. The numbers under the vertices are `dist`.
Vertex 0 is the closest unsettled vertex, so its distance is final.
Through 0, vertex 1 can be reached in 4 and vertex 2 in 1. Both distances drop from ∞.
Going 0 → 2 → 1 costs 1 + 2 = 3, shorter than the direct edge of 4, so `dist[1]` improves. Finding a shorter way like this is called relaxing an edge.
All settled: 0, 3, 1, 8, 11. Dijkstra needs non-negative weights. With a simple scan for the closest vertex it is O(V²); with a heap (priority queue) it is O((V + E) log V).
